raised.claim: Guard 3 treats an empty *brewery* probe alone as proof of absence even when the *name* probe returned hits — i.e. when the beer exists on Untappd under a different brewery, which the prompt itself classifies as a brewery-label problem, not absence.
raised.why_it_breaks: Input: probe = { brewery: '', name: 'Bulgogi — Mad Elf' } (brewery probe empty, name probe returns the real beer under another brewery) and a not_on_untappd verdict. Because `probe.brewery === ''` short-circuits the OR, `proved` is true, the terminal class is recorded verbatim, and the row is closed as not_on_untappd even though the beer is listed on Untappd. That is the exact wrong-and-terminal outcome #377 measured (beers existing under the same/other brewery with matching ABV), and `isWebFallbackBlocked` then also stops spending web fallback on it. The guard's own test comment ('' = ran, no results; hits from other breweries are not absence) requires BOTH probes empty; the code only needs one.

raised.claim: The saturation guard checks a pre-run snapshot (`postCreationRows`) and never increments it as verdicts are pushed in the same run, so one run can attach up to TRIAGE_BATCH_LIMIT (50) rows to a single issue, far past MAX_ROWS_PER_ISSUE = 12.
raised.why_it_breaks: Input: an issue with postCreationRows = 0 and a batch of 50 verdicts all routed to `issue_number` of that one issue. Every iteration passes `target.postCreationRows >= 12` because the counter is a plain number computed before planning (`countRowsForIssue(db, i.number, i.createdAt)`) and `pushInto(byIssue, ...)` never bumps it. Result: a single comment batch dumps 50 examples into one issue — the exact magnet shape (#347: 36 rows) the guard exists to stop — and only the *next* run starts refusing.

raised.quote:
log.warn({ covered, batch: orphans.length, guardHits: plan.guardHits },
        'orphan-triage: verdict shortfall');
raised.claim: guardHits is only logged inside `if (covered < orphans.length)`, but guard refusals do not reduce `covered` — a run where every orphan gets a verdict and every verdict is refused by a guard logs no guardHits at all.
raised.why_it_breaks: Input: a batch of 50 orphans, model returns 50 valid verdicts, all routed to one saturated (or unscoped) issue. `covered` = 50 = `orphans.length`, so the shortfall warn never fires and the four counters stay invisible; the digest only shows `skipped`. This is precisely the stated purpose of guardHits ('a model looping on the same illegal proposal is visible in one line'), and it fails whenever the model is fully covering but consistently mis-routing.

raised.claim: The model-authored `issue.body` is rendered *before* our scope block, and `parseScopeBlock` takes the FIRST `triage-scope` fence in the body — so a fence inside the model's own body text silently replaces the scope we rendered from the validated structured field.
raised.why_it_breaks: Input: `new_issues[0].scope = { beer_ids: [1], where: [] }` (legal) but `body` contains ` ```triage-scope\n{"beer_ids":[],"where":[{"col":"review_class","op":"=","value":"matcher_bug"}]}\n``` ` (model hand-writing the block, copying the prompt's old example, or just quoting the format). Next run `parseScopeBlock(i.body)` returns the model's block — a class-only scope that guard 1 would have rejected — so the issue silently accepts every future matcher_bug row. The PR's invariant 'we parse our own output, not model prose' does not hold for the body half of the rendered issue.

raised.claim: Every quiet verdict that is not `not_on_untappd` increments `outcome.wontfix`, so guard 3's degraded rows (written to the DB as `matcher_bug`) are reported in the daily digest as `wontfix`.
raised.why_it_breaks: Input: one not_on_untappd verdict that fails the class gate; planTriageActions pushes `{ ...verdict, review_class: 'matcher_bug', ... }` into `plan.quiet`, then this loop counts it via the `else` branch. The digest line renders `Тріаж: … 1 wontfix`, i.e. the run reports the row as intentionally never-matching while the DB says matcher_bug and the enrichment pool keeps retrying it. The new degradation path makes this routine (every candidate-bearing not_on_untappd), and it also hides how many absences the gate actually refused.

raised.claim: The tool schema leaves `col`/`op` unconstrained (and `value` typed `['string','number','null']`) while `ScopeTermSchema` is a strict union, so a tool-schema-valid scope term fails `AnalysisSchema.parse` and takes down the whole batch.
raised.why_it_breaks: Input: the model emits `{ col: 'source_url', op: '=', value: 'x' }` or `{ col: 'candidates_count', op: '=', value: '3' }` (both legal per ANALYSIS_TOOL_SCHEMA: col string, op string, value string/number). No `ScopeTermSchema` variant matches (no `=` for TEXT_COLS; `value` must be `z.number()` for numeric cols), so the union fails and `AnalysisSchema.parse` throws on the entire `new_issues` array — a whole run of up to 50 orphans is lost/retried because one predicate on one proposed issue used a wrong op or a numeric-as-string. The prompt only prose-instructs the allowed grammar, and the drift-guard test only compares top-level `required` keys, so nothing pins the nested shape.

raised.claim: Guard 2 evaluates any scope `parseScopeBlock` returns but never applies `isLegalScope` to *existing* issues' scopes, so a class-only `where` block on an existing issue (the shape guard 1 rejects at proposal time) accepts every row of that class.
raised.why_it_breaks: Input: an open issue whose body (ops backfill, hand edit, or a body-fence hijack) carries `{"beer_ids":[],"where":[{"col":"review_class","op":"=","value":"matcher_bug"}]}` and a matcher_bug verdict for any row. `rowSatisfiesScope` evaluates the review_class term against the verdict class and returns true for every matcher_bug row, so the issue reverts to being the whole-class dumping ground (#347) while guard 1 keeps rejecting that exact shape in proposals. Nothing in the chain rejects it for existing issues.

raised.claim: The new `issueNumber` parameter defaults to null and is written unconditionally, so any caller that omits it silently wipes the v23 row→issue link that the migration exists to create.
raised.why_it_breaks: Input: a call `setEnrichFailureReview(db, id, 'matcher_bug', note, atIso)` (5 args — the pre-change signature, which still type-checks). The generated SQL sets `issue_number = NULL`, destroying the authoritative link the PR calls the fix for the unqueryable `→ #N` suffix. In the shown code `review(v, null)` already does this for quiet verdicts, so a row previously attached to an issue that is later re-triaged quiet loses its audit trail. Low confidence: I cannot see callers outside the shown files, but the defaulted parameter makes the wipe reachable from unchanged call sites.

raised.quote:
`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM enrich_failures
        WHERE issue_number = ? AND reviewed_at > ?`,
raised.claim: `reviewed_at > created_at` compares two different ISO formats — `now.toISOString()` always carries milliseconds while GitHub `created_at` never does — so text comparison mis-orders them within the same second (`.000Z` sorts before `Z`).
raised.why_it_breaks: Input: an issue created at `2026-08-14T06:00:00Z` and a row reviewed at `2026-08-14T06:00:00.500Z`. Character 19 is `.` vs `Z`, `.` < `Z`, so the row reads as pre-creation and is not counted toward `postCreationRows`, weakening the saturation guard. Same-second rows are the only mis-ordered case (a second later the comparison is correct), so the practical impact is small.

raised.quote:
reviewed_at        = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.reviewed_at END`,
raised.claim: `recordEnrichFailure`'s 0↔>0 reset clears review_class/review_note/reviewed_at but leaves the new `issue_number` set, so a re-opened row keeps a stale row→issue link that the migration introduced as the authoritative one.
raised.why_it_breaks: Input: a row attached to issue #347 (`issue_number = 347`), whose next enrichment failure flips `candidates_count` across the 0 boundary. The CASE arms NULL the review fields but `issue_number` survives, so the row re-enters the untriaged pool while still reporting as attached to #347 — the exact audit question the column was added to answer ('which rows went to this issue') now returns false positives. `countRowsForIssue` hides it only because `reviewed_at` went NULL.
